chunks: It is only what we have previously mentioned regarding taqiyyah, and nothing else.
As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from a number of our companions, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
"Concerning the one who commits īqāb: upon him is stoning if he is muḥṣan, and upon him is the hadd punishment if he is not muḥṣan."
So the correct way regarding this is in...

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation practiced to avoid harm, used here to explain how a report is to be understood
key_terms.الرَّجْمَ: stoning as a prescribed legal punishment in this context
key_terms.الْحَدُّ: the fixed legal punishment applied in this case when the person is not muḥṣan
key_terms.مُحْصَنًا: legally protected through valid marital status, affecting the applicable punishment
key_terms.يُوقِبُ: commits the act of penetration referred to in the legal discussion

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for the one who commits liwāṭ if he is muḥṣan or non-muḥṣan?
ai.summary: This passage discusses a legal ruling related to liwāṭ and distinguishes the punishment based on whether the offender is muḥṣan or not. It also indicates that a preceding report is to be understood in light of taqiyyah, reflecting juristic reconciliation of narrations in Shia hadith scholarship.
